reasons.plausibility: Pre-oxidation of a highly reactive, multi-principal element alloy like HfNbTaTiZr at 1000°C is unlikely to form a protective, adherent oxide; it will likely produce a thick, porous, non-protective scale that spalls and embrittles the substrate, contradicting known oxidation behavior of refractory alloys.
reasons.testability: The proposed falsification test is clear and well-structured, directly comparing oxidation mass gain and post-exposure mechanical properties of treated vs. untreated specimens, providing a decisive criterion.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a fundamentally flawed mechanism (protective pre-oxidation) for a material class known for catastrophic oxidation, offering a misleading direction for solving the oxygen resistance problem.
